move.text:
Dear customer,

We have reviewed your offer and can adjust our Angebot as follows. We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account. Furthermore, we appreciate the updated demand forecast, which allows us to adjust our pricing accordingly. We are pleased to accept your proposed 24-month contract term and 45-day payment terms. In consideration of these updated terms and the increased volume, we can offer a revised price of €5.53 per unit. 

To outline our offer clearly, we can provide a price of €5.53 per unit, Zahlungsziel 45 days net, a contract term of 24 months. Please note that our general terms and conditions apply; the quote lists our standard terms, and our standard Zahlungsziel is 30 days net. 

A binding higher volume would help us and can improve the price. Which volume can you commit to? Our offer remains valid for 30 days.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Franz Stadler
Inside Sales, Schraubenhandel Leitner & Sohn GmbH

Dear customer,

Thank you very much for your continued partnership with Schraubenhandel Leitner & Sohn GmbH. We appreciate your acceptance of the 60-day payment term and the 36-month contract duration.

As no further data was provided to support a larger reduction, we can only make a modest adjustment to our pricing. For this final offer (letztes Angebot), we propose a revised price of €5.38 per unit under these agreed terms. To outline the complete terms of our offer, we present a price of €5.38 per unit, Zahlungsziel 60 days net, a contract term of 36 months. Please note that our price follows our main cost drivers: PPI-C2594, LCI-C.

This is our final offer (letztes Angebot). Please decide. This Angebot stays valid for 7 days. We hope to continue serving your business from our extensive range!

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Franz Stadler
Inside Sales, Schraubenhandel Leitner & Sohn GmbH

decisions.tactician: Every option sits at the same level to the supplier (about -16%), so the choice comes down to our cost and how well the terms fit its needs. o5 (45 d, 24 months) gives our lowest C, €290,795. Its 24-month term covers the horizon and offers the planning security it wants. Asking for less stretch on payment than o1/o2 (90 d) or E0 (60 d) costs us nothing in C, and the three forecast-growth arguments speak to its main need for volume. I left out the delivery-record argument: the supplier can walk away easily, and pressing on reliability while asking for volume could sour things. 12-month options cost far more.

decisions.tactician: o2 gives us essentially the lowest C (€303,393, against E0's €303,437 and o8's €303,237, all nearly equal). It also offers the supplier something it values but the pricing does not count: a 36-month commitment that secures its shift. That makes acceptance or a further price move more likely than with E0. The delivery-record argument is a new kind and adds pressure. Accepting at €5.53 now would leave a large improvement on the table, since it is still moving about €0.25 per reply.

decisions.tactician: E0 keeps the terms it proposed itself (60 d, 36 months) and moves only on price, which is the easiest step for its committee to approve. Its C (€311k) is close to the lowest-C options. o1 and o2 save only about €450 but switch to 14 d payment, which reshuffles terms without real gain. The 24-month variants give up the planning security it values. Its pace (€0.18 per reply) suggests it can reach this level within about one round. We still hold acceptable sheets, so we keep a fallback. No new arguments are available to cite.
